metadata.title: Syntactic System and Clause Typology of Kangra Gaddi

word_order.with_adjuncts: Subject - Indirect Object - Direct Object - Verb
word_order.modifiers: Preverbal and prenominal (modifiers precede nouns and verbs)
word_order.scrambling: Freely permitted for discourse functions; fronted object encodes contrastive focus

main_clause_types.structure: Formed by inserting question particle 'kɛ' clause-initially or clause-finally (e.g. 'kɛ tusɛ ədʒ əkhbɑr pəɽ-i' / 'tusɛ ədʒ əkhbɑr pəɽ-i kɛ')
Wh-in-situ (wh-word replaces questioned constituent without fronting)
Second-person subject typically dropped; verb inflects with -ɑ (m), -i (f), -ɛ (pl/hon)

subordinate_clause_types.structure: Correlative construction: relative pronoun 'dʒes' / 'dʒəs' in relative clause + correlative pronoun 'so' / 'təssɑ' in main clause
subordinate_clause_types.reduced_form: Relative clause directly precedes modified noun without pronouns

subordinate_clause_types.structure: Marked with infinitival suffix -nɑ / -ɳɑ (e.g. 'rəso kər-n-ɑ pəsənd hɑ')
Nominal or verbal coordination with conjunctions 'tɛ' / 'ətɛ' ('and'), 'pər' ('but')

core_syntactic_relations.wh_in_situ: Wh-words remain in base structural position; fronting is scrambling for focus, not syntactic movement
core_syntactic_relations.wh_scope_marking: Direct question reading out of finite complement clauses requires scope marker 'kɛ' in matrix clause (Riemsdijk 1982); single scope marker used for multiple embedded wh-words
core_syntactic_relations.wh_extraction_prohibition: Syntactic wh-extraction out of finite complement clauses is strictly ungrammatical (*kɛ rɑm dʒɑɳ-d-ɑ hɑ dʒe sitɛ khə-u?)

negation_markers.distribution: Prohibitive marker used in negative imperatives

tam_interactions.perfective: Negative marker either precedes main verb or intervenes between main verb and past auxiliary
tam_interactions.imperfective: Negative marker always precedes main verb; indicative copula 'hɑ' is barred when negated
tam_interactions.progressive: Negative marker precedes main verb or precedes progressive auxiliary 'kər-'
tam_interactions.modals: Negative marker can precede or follow main verb with modal 'səkɳɑ' ('can')
tam_interactions.complex_predicates: Negative marker can precede either main verb or light verb

information_structure.focus: Immediate preverbal position in canonical order

focus_particles.function: Restrictive focus ('only') / emphasis; attaches to any category
